chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the dowry (sadaq), so he said: 'It is what people agree upon, or twelve ounces and a Nash, or five hundred dirhams.' And he said: 'The ounce is forty dirhams, and the Nash is twenty dirhams.'

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةً: A unit of weight/money (ounce), defined here as 40 dirhams
key_terms.الصَّدَاقِ: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.النَّشَّ: A smaller unit of weight/money, defined here as 20 dirhams
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: A silver coin/currency unit used in the definition of the dowry values

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and standard value of the Islamic dowry (sadaq) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of the dowry (mahr) by prioritizing mutual consent ('taradhi') while offering specific historical monetary standards as benchmarks. It defines the 'ounce' and 'Nash' in terms of dirhams, reflecting the economic context of the early Shia scholarly tradition where silver dirhams served as the primary unit of value. This establishes a dual framework: the ideal of voluntary agreement supported by tangible, calculable minimums to prevent ambiguity in marital contracts.
